cards.name: PathPoint
cards.path: Classes for working with art path items/PathPoint
cards.summary: Read-only view of one anchor point of an existing Photoshop path: its anchor position, the two Bezier direction handles and whether it is a corner or smooth point.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.pathItems[i].subPathItems[j].pathPoints[k]. It only reports geometry; to build a path you fill PathPointInfo objects and pass them to pathItems.add().

key_members.name: anchor
key_members.use: anchor position [x, y] of the point

key_members.name: leftDirection
key_members.use: incoming Bezier handle; equals anchor on a straight segment

key_members.name: rightDirection
key_members.use: outgoing Bezier handle; equals anchor on a straight segment

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the SubPathItem the point belongs to

gotchas: Every property is read-only: you cannot move a point in place; rebuild the path from PathPointInfo objects and add it again.

Coordinates come back in points measured against the document resolution, so on a non-72 ppi document they do not equal pixel positions (unverified; common workaround: read at 72 ppi or convert with the resolution).
use_for: copy a logo outline's points into another tool
measure a pen-tool path to place type or shapes along it
audit a clipping path before print
avoid: editing a path point by point: rebuild it with PathPointInfo + pathItems.add instead

cards.name: PathPointInfo
cards.path: Classes for working with art path items/PathPointInfo
cards.summary: Script-side description of one path point (anchor plus left and right direction handles plus corner/smooth kind) used as input when a script creates a path; it is not a live object in the document.
cards.how: Create with new PathPointInfo(), set anchor / leftDirection / rightDirection as [x, y] arrays and kind, collect them in a SubPathInfo.entireSubPath array, then pass the SubPathInfo array to app.activeDocument.pathItems.add(name, ...).

key_members.name: leftDirection
key_members.use: incoming handle [x, y]; set equal to anchor for a straight segment

key_members.name: rightDirection
key_members.use: outgoing handle [x, y]; set equal to anchor for a straight segment

key_members.name: kind
key_members.use: PointKind.CORNERPOINT for sharp corners, PointKind.SMOOTHPOINT for curves

gotchas: All three coordinates must be set even for straight lines: copy the anchor into both handles.

Coordinates are interpreted in points against the document resolution, so pixel coordinates land scaled on a non-72 ppi document (unverified; usual fix is to divide by resolution/72 or temporarily work at 72 ppi).
The object does nothing on its own: nothing appears until pathItems.add() is called with the SubPathInfo array.
use_for: draw a badge, arrow or frame outline from code
build a vector mask or clipping path from computed coordinates
turn data (chart lines) into Photoshop paths
avoid: reading an existing path: use PathPoint via subPathItems[].pathPoints

cards.name: SubPathInfo
cards.path: Classes for working with art path items/SubPathInfo
cards.summary: Script-side description of one contour of a new path: its array of PathPointInfo points, whether it is closed and how it combines with the other contours (add, subtract, intersect, exclude).
cards.how: Create with new SubPathInfo(), set entireSubPath to an array of PathPointInfo, closed and operation, then pass an array of SubPathInfo objects to app.activeDocument.pathItems.add(name, subPaths).

key_members.name: entireSubPath
key_members.use: array of PathPointInfo objects in drawing order

key_members.name: closed
key_members.use: true closes the contour back to its first point (needed to fill or select it)

key_members.name: operation
key_members.use: ShapeOperation.SHAPEADD / SHAPESUBTRACT / SHAPEINTERSECT / SHAPEXOR against the other contours

gotchas: entireSubPath must be an Array of PathPointInfo even though the dictionary types it as a single PathPointInfo.
pathItems.add expects an array of SubPathInfo, not a single SubPathInfo, even for one contour.
operation controls how overlapping contours make holes (for example a ring = outer SHAPEADD + inner SHAPESUBTRACT); leaving it unset gives an unclear default (unverified).
use_for: build a multi-contour path such as a ring or a cut-out letter
create a closed selection shape to fill or mask
generate clipping paths for product cut-outs
avoid: inspecting an existing path: use SubPathItem

review.changes: example called pt() defined only on the PathPointInfo card; made it self-contained

cards.name: SubPathItem
cards.path: Classes for working with art path items/SubPathItem
cards.summary: Read-only view of one contour inside an existing Photoshop path: whether it is closed, how it combines with sibling contours and its collection of path points.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.pathItems[i].subPathItems[j]. Use it to inspect geometry; to make paths use SubPathInfo with pathItems.add().

key_members.name: pathPoints
key_members.use: the PathPoints collection of this contour

key_members.name: closed
key_members.use: true when the contour is closed

key_members.name: operation
key_members.use: ShapeOperation this contour applies to the others (add, subtract, intersect, xor)

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the PathItem that owns the contour

gotchas: Every property is read-only; to change a contour rebuild the whole path with SubPathInfo objects.
A path made of several shapes (a letter with a counter, a ring) has several sub paths; do not assume subPathItems[0] is the whole outline.
use_for: check that every contour of a clipping path is closed before export
count shapes in a traced logo path
copy path geometry to another document or app
avoid: creating or editing contours: use SubPathInfo

cards.name: Notifier
cards.summary: One registered event handler: when the given Photoshop event (for example document open or new document) fires, Photoshop runs the attached script file. It is the scripting side of File > Scripts > Script Events Manager.
cards.how: Created through app.notifiers.add(event, file, eventClass); each entry of app.notifiers is a Notifier. Nothing fires unless app.notifiersEnabled is true.

key_members.name: event
key_members.use: four-character event ID or string ID the handler listens for, e.g. 'Opn ' or 'Mk  '

key_members.name: eventClass
key_members.use: optional class filter, e.g. 'Dcmn' so 'Mk  ' only fires for new documents

key_members.name: eventFile
key_members.use: the script file (File) that runs when the event fires

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the Application (the object that owns app.notifiers) (unverified)

gotchas: Events raised while a script is running generally do not trigger notifiers (they happen inside a 'play script' event), so a pipeline that opens files by script will not fire its own open handler.
All properties are read-only: to change the event or file, remove the notifier and add a new one.
Notifiers persist across Photoshop restarts like Script Events Manager entries, so a test handler left behind keeps firing for the user (unverified).
use_for: auto-apply a colour profile check or watermark when a document opens
log or tag every new document for a brand pipeline
avoid: unattended pipelines that open files by script: the handler will not fire; call the step directly

review.changes: eventFile said '(or action)': the batch only gives a file to execute; parent now names the Application, marked unverified

cards.name: ArtLayers
cards.summary: The collection of non-group layers (pixel, text, adjustment, smart object, fill) directly inside a document or layer group, with methods to add a new empty layer and find layers by name or index.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.artLayers (top level only) or someLayerSet.artLayers for layers inside a group.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: create a new empty layer and return it

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: first art layer with that exact name

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of art layers in this container

key_members.name: removeAll
key_members.use: delete every art layer in this container

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the Document or LayerSet that owns the collection

gotchas: Only covers layers directly in this container: layers inside groups are not listed, walk layerSets recursively or use the group's own artLayers.
getByName raises an error when nothing matches instead of returning null (unverified); wrap it in try/catch.
add() inserts relative to the active layer, so set the active layer first if position matters (unverified).
use_for: add an empty layer for a texture, glow or text in a poster build
find the hero photo layer of a template by name
loop over a template's layers to swap content
avoid: listing groups too: use Layers (art layers and layer sets together)

review.changes: add() key_member stated 'above the active layer' as fact while the gotcha marks it unverified; key_member no longer claims a position

cards.name: Channels
cards.summary: The collection of a document's channels: the colour component channels (for example Red, Green, Blue) plus any alpha (saved selection) and spot colour channels.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.channels; add() creates a new alpha channel.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: create a new alpha channel and return it

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: channel by name, e.g. 'Red' or a saved mask name
channel by index; component channels come first

gotchas: Component channels cannot be deleted, so removeAll on an RGB/CMYK document will not leave an empty collection and may raise an error (unverified).
Channel names are localised in non-English Photoshop builds ('Red' may not exist); prefer indices for component channels.
The composite channel (RGB / CMYK) is not an entry of the collection (unverified).
use_for: save a subject selection as an alpha channel for later masking
read a single colour channel to build a luminosity mask
check a print file for stray alpha or spot channels
avoid: layer masks: those live on the layer, not in Channels

review.changes: example stored a selection that may not exist; added selection.selectAll() first

cards.name: ColorSamplers
cards.summary: The document's colour sampler markers (Color Sampler tool points) whose colour values appear in the Info panel; the collection adds a new sampler at a position.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.colorSamplers; add(position) takes an [x, y] UnitValue pair and returns a ColorSampler.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: place a new sampler at [x, y] and return it

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of samplers in the document

gotchas: Photoshop caps the number of samplers per document and add() fails past the cap (unverified; the cap is not in the harvest).
Plain numbers in the position are read in the current ruler units; pass UnitValue(..., 'px') to be explicit.
The ExtendScript dictionary lists no removeAll on this collection (the COM type library does: ColorSamplers.RemoveAll); in a .jsx use ColorSampler.removeAll or call remove() on each sampler.
use_for: read exact colours at fixed points for a brand colour check
measure skin or product tones before and after a grade
avoid: averaging an area: samplers read a point (or the tool's sample size), not a region

review.changes: removed the invented '10 samplers' cap; the 'no removeAll' gotcha ignored the batch's COM RemoveAll and the element's removeAll, rewritten

cards.name: CountItems
cards.summary: The document's Count tool markers (numbered dots used to count objects in an image); the collection adds a marker at a position.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.countItems; add(position) takes an [x, y] pair and returns a CountItem.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: place a numbered count marker at [x, y]

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: how many count markers the document holds

gotchas: Count markers are non-printing annotations; they do not appear in exported pixels.
Markers belong to Count groups in the UI; how scripted markers choose a group is not exposed here (unverified).
use_for: mark and number items on a product sheet or proof for review
read how many items a reviewer counted
avoid: visible numbered callouts on the design: draw text layers instead, count markers do not print

cards.name: Documents
cards.summary: The collection of documents open in Photoshop; add() creates a new document with size, resolution, colour mode, fill, bit depth and profile.
cards.how: Reach it as app.documents; the new document from add() becomes app.activeDocument.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: new document: width, height, resolution, name, mode, initialFill, pixelAspectRatio, bitsPerChannel, colorProfileName

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: open document by its window name

gotchas: Plain numbers for width/height are read in the current ruler units (app.preferences.rulerUnits); pass UnitValue(1080, 'px') to get pixels regardless of preferences.
Open documents may belong to the user or another pipeline: never close or modify a document you did not open; create your own and close only that.
colorProfileName must match an installed profile name exactly or the call fails (unverified).
use_for: create a social post, poster or banner canvas at an exact size
set up a CMYK print document at 300 ppi
find an already open template by name
avoid: opening a file: use app.open(File(...)), not documents.add

cards.name: Guides
cards.summary: The document's ruler guides; add() places a new horizontal or vertical guide at a coordinate.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.guides; add(Direction.VERTICAL | Direction.HORIZONTAL, coordinate) returns a Guide.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: new guide: direction plus coordinate from the image origin

gotchas: Pass the coordinate as UnitValue(..., 'px'); a plain number is read in the current ruler units.

This harvest lists no index accessor or removeAll on Guides; index access (guides[i]) works in practice (unverified). Remove guides one by one with Guide.remove; Guide also lists removeAll (unverified whether it clears every guide).
Guides are non-printing and do not survive export to flat formats.
use_for: lay out margins, safe zones and centre lines on a social or print template
mark bleed and trim for print
avoid: visible layout lines in the output: draw shape layers instead

review.changes: gotcha said guides can only be removed one by one; the batch lists removeAll on Guide, now mentioned

cards.name: HistoryStates
cards.summary: Read-only list of the document's History panel states (and snapshots); used to inspect or roll back to an earlier state.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.historyStates; jump back by assigning one of its entries to app.activeDocument.activeHistoryState.

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: history state by its step name, e.g. 'Gaussian Blur'

gotchas: There is no add(): states are created by edits; the number kept is capped by the History States preference, so old states roll off during long scripts.
Each scripted step adds its own state; wrap a whole script in Document.suspendHistory to collapse it into one undoable step.
Step names are localised and repeat (several 'Gaussian Blur' states), so getByName returns the first match only.
use_for: try a look and roll back if a check fails
render variants from one base state without reopening the file
avoid: long-term versioning: save files or layer comps instead, history is lost on close

cards.name: LayerComps
cards.summary: The document's layer comps: saved snapshots of layer visibility, position and appearance (styles) that can be re-applied to switch between design variants.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.layerComps; add(name, comment, appearance, position, visibility) records the current layer state.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: record the current layer state as a named comp; flags choose which aspects are captured

gotchas: A comp only records visibility, position and appearance (layer style) for the flags you pass; pixel and text content changes are not captured.
Comps can be invalidated (warning icon) when layers are deleted or merged after recording (unverified as a scripting error).
use_for: keep A/B variants of an ad or thumbnail in one PSD
export several layouts (square, story) from one master file
avoid: variants that differ in text or pixels: comps do not store content, use separate layers or files

cards.name: Layers
cards.summary: The collection of all top-level layers of a document or group, art layers and layer groups (layer sets) together, in stacking order.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.layers or someLayerSet.layers. Items are ArtLayer or LayerSet; check typename. There is no add(): use artLayers.add() or layerSets.add().

key_members.use: layer by index, 0 = top of the stack

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of layers at this level

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: first layer (art layer or group) with that name

key_members.name: removeAll
key_members.use: delete every layer at this level

gotchas: Only one level deep: layers inside groups appear under that group's own layers collection, so walk recursively for a full tree.
No add(): new layers come from artLayers.add() or layerSets.add().
Iterating a large layers collection via the DOM is slow; Action Manager descriptors are much faster for big files (unverified for 27.4).
use_for: walk a template PSD to find placeholders
list a file's layer structure for QC before export
avoid: creating layers: use ArtLayers or LayerSets

cards.name: LayerSets
cards.summary: The collection of layer groups (folders in the Layers panel) directly inside a document or group; add() creates a new empty group.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.layerSets or someLayerSet.layerSets for nested groups.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: create a new empty layer group and return it

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of groups at this level

key_members.name: removeAll
key_members.use: delete every group (and its contents) at this level

gotchas: Only lists groups at one level; nested groups live in each group's own layerSets.
removeAll deletes the groups together with all layers inside them.
To put new layers inside a group, add them through the group's own artLayers / layerSets rather than moving them afterwards.
use_for: organise a generated poster into Background / Subject / Type groups
find the group that holds a template's swappable content
avoid: listing all layers: use Layers

cards.name: Notifiers
cards.summary: The application's list of registered event handlers (Script Events Manager entries); add() registers a script to run when a Photoshop event fires.
cards.how: Reach it as app.notifiers (the dictionary says 'in the document', but it hangs off the Application). Turn on app.notifiersEnabled for any of them to fire.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: register: event ID, script File, optional event class

gotchas: Nothing fires while app.notifiersEnabled is false.
Events produced by scripts generally do not trigger notifiers.
removeAll also deletes handlers the user set up in Script Events Manager; remove only the ones you added.
use_for: auto-run a brand setup script whenever a new document is created
auto-check files when a designer opens them
avoid: scripted batch runs: call the step directly instead of relying on an event

cards.name: PathItems
cards.summary: The document's paths (the Paths panel entries: saved paths, work path, vector mask and clipping paths); add() creates a new named path from SubPathInfo data.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.pathItems; add(name, subPathInfoArray) returns a PathItem you can select, fill, stroke or make a clipping path.

key_members.name: add
key_members.use: create a named path from an array of SubPathInfo

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: path by its Paths panel name

gotchas: add() needs an array of SubPathInfo (each with a PathPointInfo array), not plain coordinates.
Path coordinates are scaled by document resolution (points vs pixels) on non-72 ppi files (unverified).
A shape layer's vector mask is listed among the paths only while that layer is selected (unverified).
use_for: build a clipping path for a product cut-out
turn a computed outline into a selection to fill or mask
check a supplied image for an existing clipping path
avoid: vector shape layers with fill: a path alone does not render; fill or stroke it, or use a shape layer

review.changes: example used an undefined sp variable; now builds its own SubPathInfo so it runs

cards.name: PathPoints
cards.summary: Read-only collection of the PathPoint objects that make up one sub path of an existing path.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.pathItems[i].subPathItems[j].pathPoints.

key_members.use: point by index in drawing order

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of points in the sub path

key_members.name: getByName
key_members.use: point by name (points rarely have useful names)

gotchas: No add or remove: the points of an existing path cannot be edited through this collection; rebuild the path with PathPointInfo.
Coordinates of the points are in points, not pixels, on non-72 ppi documents (unverified).
cards.example:
var pts = app.activeDocument.pathItems[0].subPathItems[0].pathPoints;
for (var i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) $.writeln(pts[i].anchor);
use_for: export a Photoshop path's points to another tool
measure a path's bounding points for layout
avoid: creating paths: use PathPointInfo + SubPathInfo + pathItems.add

cards.name: SubPathItems
cards.summary: Read-only collection of the contours (SubPathItem objects) that make up one existing path.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.pathItems[i].subPathItems.

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: number of contours in the path

gotchas: Read-only: contours cannot be added or removed here; rebuild the path with SubPathInfo objects.
Contour order follows drawing order, not visual position.
use_for: count the separate shapes in a traced path
loop contours to copy a path's geometry
avoid: creating contours: use SubPathInfo

cards.name: TextFonts
cards.summary: The collection of fonts installed and available to Photoshop, each a TextFont with name, family, style and PostScript name.
cards.how: Reach it as app.fonts. Use it to resolve a family/style to the PostScript name that TextItem.font expects.
gotchas: TextItem.font takes the PostScript name (e.g. 'Montserrat-Bold'), not the family name shown in menus; look it up here first.
Which name getByName matches (display name or PostScript name) is not stated in the dictionary; loop and compare family/style when unsure (unverified).
Looping the whole collection is slow on machines with many fonts; cache the result for a run.
Adobe Fonts activated after Photoshop started may not appear until restart (unverified).
use_for: verify a brand font is installed before building a poster
pick the exact weight for a headline text layer
avoid: assuming a family name works as TextItem.font: always resolve the PostScript name

cards.name: CMYKColor
cards.summary: CMYK ink-percentage colour (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, each 0 to 100), usually used as the cmyk part of a SolidColor.
cards.how: Normally reached as someSolidColor.cmyk (setting it switches the SolidColor to CMYK); can also be created with new CMYKColor() and assigned to solidColor.cmyk.
gotchas: Values are percentages 0-100, not 0-255 or 0-1.
Reading .cmyk from an RGB SolidColor gives a converted value that depends on Edit > Color Settings, so it may not match a printer's spec.
Rich black for print must be set explicitly by adding cyan, magenta and yellow under black; black = 100 with the other inks at 0 is plain K.
use_for: set exact brand ink values for print fills
specify rich black for large print areas
avoid: screen-only work: use RGBColor / hexValue

review.changes: removed the invented 60/40/40/100 rich-black recipe (not in the batch)

cards.name: Color
cards.summary: Abstract base type of Photoshop's colour classes (RGBColor, CMYKColor, GrayColor, HSBColor, LabColor, NoColor); it has no members of its own.
cards.how: Never constructed or used directly; it is the declared superclass. Work with SolidColor and its rgb / cmyk / hsb / lab / gray parts.

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: no harvested members: abstract base type only; use SolidColor or a concrete colour class

gotchas: new Color() is not a useful object; build colours with new SolidColor() (unverified that the constructor throws).
cards.example:
var c = app.foregroundColor; // a SolidColor
if (c.model == ColorModel.RGB) $.writeln(c.rgb.hexValue);
use_for: type documentation only: knowing which classes count as a colour
avoid: any direct use: use SolidColor

cards.name: GrayColor
cards.summary: Grayscale colour with one value, gray, from 0 to 100, used as the gray part of a SolidColor.
cards.how: Normally reached as someSolidColor.gray; setting gray.gray switches the SolidColor model to grayscale.
gotchas: The value reads like a K (ink) percentage, so 100 is black and 0 is white, the opposite of an RGB brightness (unverified).
The final grey a value produces depends on the document's gray working space (dot gain).
use_for: set neutral greys for mono print jobs
fill grayscale masks with an exact tone
avoid: colour designs: use RGBColor or CMYKColor

cards.name: HSBColor
cards.summary: Hue / saturation / brightness colour (hue 0-360 degrees, saturation and brightness 0-100), used as the hsb part of a SolidColor.
cards.how: Reached as someSolidColor.hsb; setting its values switches the SolidColor to HSB, and .rgb / .cmyk then give converted values.
gotchas: Photoshop documents have no HSB mode; the colour is converted to the document's mode when used.
Hue is in degrees 0-360 while saturation and brightness are percentages.
use_for: generate harmonious palettes by rotating hue
make tints and shades of a brand colour by changing brightness
avoid: exact print specs: use CMYKColor

cards.name: LabColor
cards.summary: CIE Lab colour (L lightness 0-100, A and B from -128 to 127), device-independent, used as the lab part of a SolidColor.
cards.how: Reached as someSolidColor.lab; setting L / A / B switches the SolidColor to Lab.
gotchas: Property names are upper-case L, A, B; lower-case .l / .a / .b are not the harvested names.
Lab values outside the document's gamut are clipped when the colour is used in RGB or CMYK.
use_for: match a measured brand colour given in Lab
compare colour differences device-independently
avoid: simple screen colours: use RGBColor.hexValue

cards.name: NoColor
cards.summary: Represents a missing colour (no colour); it has no members of its own and Photoshop's DOM rarely uses it.
cards.how: Created with new NoColor() (the COM type library marks it creatable). Where Photoshop properties accept or return it is not documented in the harvest.

key_members.name: NoColor
key_members.use: no harvested members: the constructor new NoColor() is the whole API

gotchas: Unlike Illustrator, Photoshop has no 'none' fill on layers through this class; to show no fill hide or delete the layer or set its fill opacity to 0 (unverified that any Photoshop property accepts NoColor).
cards.example: var none = new NoColor(); // the constructor is the whole harvested API
use_for: recognising a 'no colour' value read back from a script
avoid: removing a fill in Photoshop: hide the layer or set fill opacity to 0 instead

cards.name: RGBColor
cards.summary: RGB colour with red, green and blue channels 0-255 plus a hexValue string, used as the rgb part of a SolidColor.
cards.how: Reached as someSolidColor.rgb; set either the three channels or hexValue. Setting it switches the SolidColor to RGB.
gotchas: hexValue takes six hex digits without the leading '#' (unverified whether '#' is rejected or ignored).
Channels use the 0-255 scale even in 16- and 32-bit documents.
Values can be fractional; round before comparing colours.
use_for: apply a brand hex colour to fills, text and strokes
read back a sampled colour as hex for a style guide
avoid: print ink specs: use CMYKColor

cards.name: DocumentPrintSettings
cards.summary: The document's print settings: printer, copies, colour handling and print profile, rendering intent, page position and scale, and printer marks (crop marks, registration marks, colour bars, labels).
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.printSettings; set the properties, then print with the Document's print methods.

key_members.name: activePrinter
key_members.use: name of the printer to use

key_members.name: printers
key_members.use: read-only list of available printer names

key_members.name: colorHandling
key_members.use: PrintColorHandling: printer manages, Photoshop manages, or separations

key_members.name: printSpace
key_members.use: printer colour profile name, or nothing for the source space

key_members.name: renderIntent
key_members.use: colour conversion intent when the print space differs

key_members.name: setPagePosition
key_members.use: position (DocPositionStyle), posX, posY and scale of the image on the page

gotchas: docPosition, posX, posY and scale are read-only; change placement through setPagePosition.
Printing is a side effect that cannot be undone: never send a print from an unattended run without the user's go-ahead.
activePrinter must match a name in printers exactly (unverified).
use_for: prepare a proof print with crop and registration marks
set colour-managed printing with a paper profile
avoid: PDF output for a print shop: save as Photoshop PDF instead of printing

cards.name: global
cards.summary: The ExtendScript global scope inside Photoshop: the app object plus standard JavaScript globals (eval, parseInt, URI encoding) and the alert / confirm / prompt dialogs and BridgeTalk.
cards.how: Available everywhere in a Photoshop .jsx without a prefix; app is the entry point to the whole DOM.

key_members.name: app
key_members.use: the Photoshop Application object, root of the DOM

key_members.name: decodeURIComponent
key_members.use: decode a percent-encoded payload sent over COM

key_members.name: encodeURIComponent
key_members.use: percent-encode a result string before returning it

key_members.name: uneval
key_members.use: serialise an object to source text for returning structured results

key_members.name: BridgeTalk
key_members.use: send scripts to other Adobe apps

gotchas: alert, confirm and prompt are modal: in a COM or command-line driven run they block until someone clicks, which looks like a hang.
ExtendScript is ES3: no JSON object by default, no let/const or arrow functions; use uneval/eval or a bundled JSON polyfill.
Payloads with backslashes and quotes get mangled crossing COM; send them percent-encoded and run eval(decodeURIComponent(...)) first.
use_for: entry point for every automation script
safe payload transfer from a Python or Node pipeline into Photoshop
avoid: user dialogs (alert/confirm/prompt) in unattended runs: return values instead

review.changes: example read an undefined PAYLOAD variable; it now defines one so the snippet runs

cards.name: Guide
cards.summary: One ruler guide in a document: its orientation and its distance from the image origin, editable and removable.
cards.how: Returned by app.activeDocument.guides.add(...) or read from the document's guides collection.

key_members.name: coordinate
key_members.use: UnitValue position from the image origin

gotchas: coordinate is a UnitValue; compare with .as('px') rather than as a raw number.
removeAll is listed on the single guide object; whether it clears every guide in the document is not confirmed (unverified).
use_for: move a centre or margin guide when resizing a template
clean up temporary guides after a layout script
avoid: anything that must print: guides never render

cards.name: SolidColor
cards.summary: Photoshop's general colour value: one object that holds a colour and exposes it in every model (RGB, CMYK, Lab, HSB, gray) plus the nearest web-safe colour.
cards.how: Create with new SolidColor() and set one model part (e.g. c.rgb.hexValue); read from app.foregroundColor / app.backgroundColor and pass to fills, strokes, text colour and filters that take a colour.

key_members.name: rgb
key_members.use: RGBColor view; set red/green/blue or hexValue

key_members.name: model
key_members.use: ColorModel the colour was defined in

gotchas: Setting any sub-model switches model; reading another model returns a converted value that depends on Edit > Color Settings.
Assigning to a property such as app.foregroundColor stores a copy: changing the SolidColor afterwards does not update the foreground colour.
isEqual compares colours, not models; an RGB and a CMYK definition of 'the same' colour may still differ after conversion (unverified).
use_for: set fill, text and stroke colours from a brand palette
convert a hex colour to CMYK ink values for print notes
avoid: exact conversions for press: get CMYK values from the print vendor's profile instead of Photoshop's default settings

cards.name: Point
cards.summary: Two-element coordinate (x/left, y/top) declared by the DOM for point arguments; in practice Photoshop scripts pass a plain [x, y] array.
cards.how: Not usually constructed: wherever the dictionary says Point (e.g. ArtLayer.adjustCurves, path handles) pass an array [x, y] or an array of such pairs.
gotchas: Photoshop methods accept plain arrays where Point is declared; x/left and y/top are aliases of the two elements (unverified that new Point() is constructible in Photoshop).
Units depend on context: pixels/ruler units for positions, 0-255 levels for curve points.
use_for: passing curve points to adjustCurves for an S-curve contrast boost
passing path handle coordinates
avoid: UnitValue-typed positions: colour samplers and count items take a UnitPoint pair, guides a single UnitValue

review.changes: avoid said guides take UnitValue pairs; Guides.add takes one UnitValue coordinate

cards.name: Rectangle
cards.summary: Four-element rectangle (left, top, right, bottom) with x/y/width/height aliases, as declared by the DOM for bounds-like values.
cards.how: Seen as the shape of bounds values; the dictionary types Layer.bounds and Selection.bounds as UnitRect, which come back as a four-element array [left, top, right, bottom] of UnitValue.
gotchas: Photoshop bounds are returned as arrays of UnitValue, so element math needs .as('px') or the current ruler units (unverified that a Rectangle object is ever returned instead of an Array).
Order is left, top, right, bottom, not x, y, width, height.
use_for: measure a layer to centre or align it on the canvas
fit text or logos inside a safe zone
avoid: assuming width/height elements: compute them from right - left and bottom - top

review.changes: how now says bounds are typed UnitRect in the harvest, not Rectangle

cards.name: ArtLayer
cards.path: Scripting commands and classes for Adobe Photoshop/ArtLayer
cards.summary: A single non-group layer (pixel, text, smart object, fill or adjustment layer) with its lock, mask and clipping properties, plus DOM methods that apply classic filters and adjustments directly to its pixels.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.activeLayer, app.activeDocument.artLayers[i] / getByName(name), or the return value of artLayers.add(). General layer properties (name, opacity, blendMode, visible, bounds, move, duplicate) come from the Layer superclass.

key_members.name: kind
key_members.use: LayerKind; set LayerKind.TEXT on a new empty layer to make it a text layer

key_members.name: textItem
key_members.use: the TextItem (contents, font, size, colour) of a text layer

key_members.name: isBackgroundLayer
key_members.use: set false to turn the locked Background into a normal layer

key_members.name: grouped
key_members.use: true clips this layer to the layer below (clipping mask)

key_members.name: applyStyle
key_members.use: apply a layer style preset by name

key_members.name: rasterize
key_members.use: convert text, shapes or smart objects to pixels

key_members.name: merge
key_members.use: merge down into the layer below

key_members.name: applyUnSharpMask
key_members.use: Unsharp Mask sharpening: amount, radius, threshold

key_members.name: applyMotionBlur
key_members.use: Motion Blur: angle (int) and radius (blur distance)

key_members.name: adjustLevels
key_members.use: Levels: input black/white/gamma and output range

key_members.name: adjustCurves
key_members.use: Curves from an array of [input, output] points

gotchas: The apply* and adjust* methods are destructive: they change pixels with no adjustment layer or smart filter, so duplicate the layer first if you need to go back.
Filters and adjustments need pixels: text, shape and smart object layers must be rasterized first or the call fails (unverified whether smart objects get a smart filter instead).
kind can only be set on an empty layer; setting LayerKind.TEXT on a layer with pixels fails.
An active selection restricts filters and adjustments to the selected area.
Only the classic filters have DOM methods; newer ones (Camera Raw, Neural Filters, Generative Fill) need Action Manager (executeAction).
use_for: add a headline text layer to a poster or thumbnail
soften or sharpen a product photo layer
quick tonal fixes (levels, curves, brightness) on a background
clip a texture to the layer below
avoid: non-destructive grading: add adjustment layers or smart filters through Action Manager instead of the adjust*/apply* methods

review.changes: applyMotionBlur use said 'angle and distance'; the harvested params are angle and radius

cards.name: BatchOptions
cards.path: Scripting commands and classes for Adobe Photoshop/BatchOptions
cards.summary: Options for app.batch (the File > Automate > Batch command): where processed files go, whether to override the action's open/save steps, file naming and error logging.
cards.how: Create with new BatchOptions(), set the properties, and pass it as the last argument of app.batch(inputFiles, actionName, actionSetName, options).

key_members.name: destinationFolder
key_members.use: output folder when destination is FOLDER

key_members.name: overrideSave
key_members.use: redirect the action's Save As steps to the destination

key_members.name: overrideOpen
key_members.use: ignore the action's Open steps and use the input files

key_members.name: fileNaming
key_members.use: array of FileNamingType parts, up to 6

key_members.name: errorFile
key_members.use: log file for errors instead of stopping on the first one

gotchas: app.batch runs a recorded action from the Actions panel: the action set and action names must already exist in Photoshop.
fileNaming takes at most 6 FileNamingType entries.
Without errorFile the batch stops at the first error and may show a dialog, which blocks an unattended run.
Leave suppressOpen and suppressProfile on for unattended runs, or open-option and profile dialogs can block the batch (unverified).
use_for: run one recorded look or resize action over a folder of product photos
batch-export social sizes with consistent naming
avoid: logic that differs per file: loop over files in the script instead of app.batch

cards.name: BitmapConversionOptions
cards.path: Scripting commands and classes for Adobe Photoshop/BitmapConversionOptions
cards.summary: Options for converting a document to 1-bit Bitmap mode: output resolution and the method (50% threshold, pattern dither, diffusion dither, halftone screen or custom pattern) with screen frequency, angle and dot shape.
cards.how: Create with new BitmapConversionOptions(), set method and its settings, and pass it to app.activeDocument.changeMode(ChangeMode.BITMAP, options).

key_members.name: method
key_members.use: BitmapConversionType: HALFTHRESHOLD, PATTERNDITHER, DIFFUSIONDITHER, HALFTONESCREEN, CUSTOMPATTERN

key_members.name: resolution
key_members.use: output resolution in pixels per inch

key_members.name: frequency
key_members.use: screen frequency, which the dictionary calls printer dots per inch, 1.0 to 999.99 (HALFTONESCREEN only)

key_members.name: angle
key_members.use: dot angle in degrees, -180 to 180 (HALFTONESCREEN only)

key_members.name: shape
key_members.use: halftone dot shape: ROUND, DIAMOND, ELLIPSE, LINE, SQUARE, CROSS

gotchas: Only a Grayscale document can be converted to Bitmap: convert RGB/CMYK to grayscale first.
The document is flattened by the conversion, and layers, adjustment layers and text are lost.
frequency, angle and shape only apply when method is HALFTONESCREEN; patternName only for CUSTOMPATTERN.
use_for: real halftone dot artwork for screen printing or risograph
1-bit line art for stamps, laser engraving or fax-style looks
diffusion-dither retro graphics
avoid: a halftone look in a colour design: use Filter > Pixelate > Color Halftone or a pattern overlay, which keep the layers

review.changes: frequency said 'lines per inch', the batch says printer dots per inch; added the batch ranges for frequency (1.0-999.99) and angle (-180 to 180)

cards.name: Channel
cards.path: Scripting commands and classes for Adobe Photoshop/Channel
cards.summary: One channel of a document: a colour component (Red, Cyan ...), an alpha channel holding a saved selection, or a spot colour channel, with its name, colour, opacity, visibility and histogram.
cards.how: Reach it as app.activeDocument.channels[i] / getByName(name) or from channels.add(); restrict edits to channels with app.activeDocument.activeChannels.

key_members.name: kind
key_members.use: ChannelType: COMPONENT, MASKEDAREA, SELECTEDAREA or SPOTCOLOR

key_members.name: color
key_members.use: display / ink colour for alpha and spot channels

key_members.name: opacity
key_members.use: overlay opacity of an alpha channel (solidity for spot channels), 0 to 100; the dictionary says valid only for masked-area or selected-area channels

key_members.name: duplicate
key_members.use: copy the channel, also into another document

key_members.name: merge
key_members.use: merge a spot channel into the colour channels

gotchas: histogram is declared as int but returns an array of 256 counts for the channel.
color is not valid on component channels, and component channels cannot be removed.
The dictionary lists duplicate twice (with relativeObject + insertionLocation, and with targetDocument); which form is used depends on the arguments passed (unverified).
use_for: save and reuse a cut-out selection as an alpha channel
check clipping in a channel's histogram before export
set up a spot (Pantone) channel for print
avoid: non-destructive masking on a layer: use the layer's mask, not an alpha channel

review.changes: example used getByName('Red'), which fails in CMYK or localised builds (the Channels card says prefer indices), and stored a selection that may not exist; opacity now carries the batch range and validity note

cards.name: ColorSampler
cards.path: Scripting commands and classes for Adobe Photoshop/ColorSampler
cards.summary: One colour sampler marker in a document: its position and the colour read at that point, movable and removable.
cards.how: Returned by app.activeDocument.colorSamplers.add([x, y]) or read from that collection.

key_members.name: color
key_members.use: read-only SolidColor sampled at the position

key_members.name: move
key_members.use: move the sampler to a new [x, y]

gotchas: color reads the composite image (all visible layers), not the active layer alone (unverified).
The sampled area follows the Color Sampler / Eyedropper sample-size setting, so the same point can read differently after that option changes (unverified).
position is read-only; use move() to reposition.
use_for: check a background is pure white for marketplace photos
verify a brand colour after export or grading
avoid: sampling many points: read pixels in bulk another way (e.g. export and analyse) instead of hundreds of samplers
